module: Start here: what the GDPR covers

lesson.title: Personal data
lesson.summary: Decide whether information is personal data, including when a person can be identified only indirectly.

blocks: **Personal data** is any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person (Article 4(1)).
The person the data is about is called the **data subject**. For Sunfield, data subjects include customers, staff and job applicants.
The GDPR protects natural persons, not companies. Recital 14 says it does not cover data about legal persons, such as a company's name, legal form and contact details.
Information about a named person who works at a company is different. A name is one of the identifiers listed in Article 4(1), so it relates to a natural person.
The GDPR does not apply to the personal data of people who have died (recital 27). EU countries may make their own rules about such data.
A person can be identified **directly**, for example by name. They can also be identified **indirectly** (Article 4(1)).

Article 4(1) lists identifiers such as an identification number, location data and an online identifier. It also lists factors specific to a person's physical, physiological, genetic, mental, economic, cultural or social identity.

To decide whether someone is identifiable, consider **all the means reasonably likely to be used**, by the holder of the data or by anyone else. This includes "singling out" one person from a group (recital 26).
Recital 26 tells you to weigh objective factors, such as the cost and time needed to identify someone and the technology available.
Recital 30 adds that online identifiers, such as IP addresses and cookie identifiers, can leave traces. Combined with other information, these traces can be used to profile and identify people.

Sunfield's loyalty card number is an identification number. Sunfield can link it to a customer's purchases and account, so the card number and purchase history are personal data, even on a list with no names.
A figure such as "1,200 rolls sold on Monday", with nothing linking it to anyone, is not information about an identifiable person.

questions.prompt: Which of these is personal data for Sunfield?

options.blocks: A customer's name with her pre-order history
options.reason: A name directly identifies a natural person, and the history relates to her.

options.blocks: The registration number of a supplier company
options.reason: Recital 14: data about a legal person is not covered.

options.blocks: The total number of rolls sold last Monday
options.reason: A total with no link to any person does not relate to an identifiable person.

variants.prompt: Which item relates to an identified or identifiable natural person?

options.blocks: The registration number of a supplier company
options.reason: Recital 14: data about a legal person is not covered.

options.blocks: The total number of rolls sold last Monday
options.reason: A total with no link to any person does not relate to an identifiable person.

options.blocks: A customer's name with her pre-order history
options.reason: A name directly identifies a natural person, and the history relates to her.

questions.prompt: Sunfield still holds records about a customer who has died. Does the GDPR apply to them?

options.blocks: Yes, exactly as for a living customer
options.reason: Recital 27 excludes the data of deceased persons.

options.blocks: Yes, for ten years after death
options.reason: The GDPR sets no such period. The ten years is invented.

options.blocks: No, though national rules may apply
options.reason: Recital 27: the GDPR does not apply, and EU countries may make rules.

variants.prompt: Does the GDPR apply to the personal data of people who have died?

options.blocks: Yes, for ten years after death
options.reason: The GDPR sets no such period. The ten years is invented.

options.blocks: No, though national rules may apply
options.reason: Recital 27: the GDPR does not apply, and EU countries may make rules.

options.blocks: Yes, exactly as for a living customer
options.reason: Recital 27 excludes the data of deceased persons.

questions.prompt: A list shows loyalty card numbers and purchases, but no names. Is it personal data?

options.blocks: Only if customers agreed to the loyalty scheme
options.reason: Consent does not change whether information is personal data.

options.blocks: Yes, if the numbers can reasonably be linked to customers
options.reason: An identification number allows indirect identification (Article 4(1), recital 26).
Indirect identification through a number is enough.

variants.prompt: Can data be personal data if it contains no names at all?

options.blocks: Yes, if the numbers can reasonably be linked to customers
options.reason: An identification number allows indirect identification (Article 4(1), recital 26).
Indirect identification through a number is enough.
